meta.axis: Es/N0 per data-modulation symbol (despread for CDMA)

Kim_L11.src: Kim, J. KICS 50(3) 2025: Link 11, 432 bits, 1/2, pi/4-QPSK; axis Es/N0 per symbol

Kim_L17.src: Kim 2025: Link 17, 1872 bits, 1/2, pi/4-QPSK; axis Es/N0 per symbol

assumptions: A1 Table 63 (DL channel interleaver) read from the PDF layout (Rec. p. 122, PDF p. 124): Link 32 M 27 N 47 Ar 13 Br 17 Ac 23 Bc 13; = lit_vde_fec.md 0.3, NOT lit_vdesat_fullsystem.md 1.5 (its Ac / Bc are wrong).

A2 Channel interleaver law applied literally: write rows (bit (m, n) = (m-1) N + n-1), row step new[m, n] = old[pr(m, n), n] with Cr(n) depending on the column, then column step new2[m, n] = new[m, pc(n, m)] with m the row index after the row step, read by columns. No test vector exists; AWGN PER does not depend on it.

A3 CRC: one CRC-32 per burst, at the end of the last FEC sub-block, over all sub-blocks' payload (A2-1.2.5 'over all fragments ... appended to the last segment', A4-4.6 'The CRC is always at the end of the packet'). crc_mode='block' (one CRC-32 per sub-block) is kept as the alternative. Single-block links (5, 11, 17, 32, 33) are not affected. Payload = k - 32 per burst (Link 32: 280 bits).

A4 Multi-block bursts (26, 34): sub-blocks concatenated in order, each followed by its zero padding (Link 26: 3 bits after its 18 tail bits), ONE scrambler run over all channel bits (re-initialised per packet), then the channel interleaver in IB consecutive blocks of L, then the burst stuffing bits (zeros, not scrambled) at the end.

A5 DS spreading (Link 32): burst bit i (syncword, pilot and data bits alike, counted from the first syncword bit) is XORed with Gold chips (8 i .. 8 i + 7) mod 2047 of SS0 (MSB of each byte first); chip 1 -> +1, 0 -> -1 ('ordinary BPSK', Fig. 10). SS0 by default (SS1 = the second satellite).

A6 Pilot grid: pilots at Ns + floor((dp - 1)/2) + i dp after each syncword start, up to (<=) the next syncword start (or the burst end) - floor((1 + dp)/2), i.e. A5-2.10's 'last pilot at d_s - (1 + d_p)/2' read as an upper bound. Reproduces the A5-2.10 Link 26 example (40, 67, ..., 2254; 31 symbols after the last pilot) and the pilot totals 180 / 2940 / 480 of Tables 10-11. For Link 32 the last pilot of a segment is at 523 (527 is off the d_p = 8 grid; an exact 527 would break the 180 total), so 7 data symbols precede each repeated syncword.

A7 Pilot value: bit 1 (BPSK / CDMA: spread like data); pi/4-QPSK: dibit 11 with the alternating map ((1+j)/sqrt2 at even, 1 at odd positions). pi/4-QPSK symbol index runs over the whole burst from the first syncword symbol.

A8 Link 32 burst = 4 syncwords x 48 at 0, 531, 1062, 1593 (the last one ends the burst) + 3 x 60 pilots + 1269 data = 1641 symbols (Table 11 'burst symbol duration'; the 1645 'symbols/burst' adds the 14 + 14 ramp chips).

A9 Eb/N0 helper: info bits = payload (k - 32 per burst), every burst symbol charged: Link 32 at Es/N0 -4.5 dB -> -4.5 + 10 log10(1641/280) = 3.18 dB (lit table); with 312 (CRC counted as info) it would be 2.71 dB.
A10 Ramps (14/14 chips, modulation 'not specified') and guard time are not transmitted; the waveform is the 1641-symbol burst through RRC (roll-off 0.25 SAT, 0.3 TER, 0.35 ASM per Tables 7-11).

A11 Pseudo-link 'M2435' (Report M.2435 4.3.1): k = 88 info bits, no CRC (frame error by genie), plain QPSK (A5-2.4 Gray quadrants, = the even pi/4-QPSK set), turbo rate 1/4 (punct 2 / tail 2 of the DVB-SH 1/4 code: XXY0Y1 tail, 24 tail bits), interleaver: the M.2092 CCSDS law with 2 x 44 and the default primes, since the DVB-SH / 3GPP2 interleaver is defined for other lengths only (L = 1146 / 12282) and its tables are not in the specs we hold; payload-only frame (no syncword / pilots).

A12 Links 33 (BPSK) and 26 / 34 (pi/4-QPSK) built from Tables 4, 10, 11, 63 with the same rules; Link 34 has no tail (decoder: unterminated trellis). Link 25 (SF 8, rate 1/2) and Links 27-31 not built.
A13 Ideal sync: known timing, CFO = 0, phase 0, unit gain, noise variance from the nominal Es/N0 (genie). The data-aided synchroniser (sync='da') is the next step and raises NotImplementedError.
